newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends down on good supply, gilts steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends down on good supply, gilts steady.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday at 3.25 percent, down from opening quotes of 4.5-5.0 on good funds supply and limited demand, dealers said on Monday.
"The banking system is flush with funds," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "No substantial outflows are expected till March 15 when the advance tax payments start going out."
Companies have till March 15 to make their advance tax payments and analysts estimate them to be between 30 billion and 50 billion rupees.
"Call money will be easy till the end of this week but I do not see rates rising much even after the tax payments as liquidity is quite good," the dealer added.
Dealers said prices of government securities were steady in thin trade.
"There was hardly any movement in prices today," said a money market dealer at a state-run bank. "Volumes were also poor. Most market players seem unwilling to build positions ahead of the year-end."
The current financial year ends on March 31.
"Some market players are also waiting to see how call money reacts to the tax payments," the dealer added.
The 12 percent 1999 government of India stock traded on Monday at 100 rupees unchanged from its last traded price while the 13.40 percent 1999 stock fell slightly to 102.01 from 102.02, dealers said.
Little action was seen in treasury bills also, they said.
Yields on treasury bills maturing in May were unchanged at 8.15 percent, dealers said.
There were no trades in certificates of deposit or commercial paper, they said.
